correctness.rationale: All t>0 and unrestricted feasible conductance allocations are covered. Rational interior construction yields two centered eigenvectors with eigenvalue Λ; the other eigenvalues exceed it, proven via exact positive Bernstein coefficients. Strictly negative Bernstein coefficients for the defining derivative show unique u for each 0<t<16. A positive rank-two Gram matrix with edge distances equal to all five prices proves a global SDP Rayleigh-trace bound; equality forces all five conductances, proving uniqueness without symmetry assumptions. The centered path vector establishes λ2≤[1+(16-t)q]/10 and the exact optimal segment at t=16. The standalone symbolic checker verifies the polynomial identities, sign coefficients, special equal-cost solution and boundary polynomial; its finite operations support but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full texts of the closest continuous-time and discrete-time optimization papers were compared by actual mathematical implication. General SDP/duality, arbitrary-cost path, and equal-cost cycle formulas are credited as prior work. The assessed novelty is the complete five-cycle single-price classification, unique below/above t=16, a nontrivial optimizer segment at t=16, and an explicit two-dimensional positive Gram certificate valid against unrestricted allocations; no inspected source states or directly implies these exact results. The search is not exhaustive and specialized unpublished or older work remains a risk.
residual_risks: No search can establish global novelty; an unlocated older specialized priced-cycle theorem, table or equivalent graph embedding result could cover the C5 formula.

Relevant early spectral-graph optimization literature including Fiedler’s minimax work was identified bibliographically but not inspected in complete full text; a decisive special-case comparison there remains uncertain.
The general priced-cycle semidefinite program is already known; originality is strictly the explicit structure and optimizer-face classification, not the optimization formulation.

value.rationale: The five-cycle is the first nontrivial odd cycle beyond the triangle: its reflection sectors yield a genuinely nontrivial two-mode critical spectral-gap optimizer. The result classifies all prices and every optimizer, with an exact topological switch to path support at t=16 and a previously non-obvious continuum of optimal rates only at the boundary. Explicit rational single-parameter rates, a sharp square-price cutoff and a global dual certificate offer a reusable diffusion-design benchmark, not a mere numerical table or substitution. Limitations to one exceptional price and five vertices are stated; no extension to all cycles is asserted.
